examGuide.title: Mental model and derivation
examGuide.body:
Runtime recurrences count all recursive subproblems plus local work. Master theorem applies to T(n)=aT(n/b)+f(n) under its conditions, not to arbitrary n−1 or √n reductions. A recursion tree exposes level work and depth. Exact answers also require base values. For nonlinear argument changes, substituting logarithmic variables can reveal a simpler recurrence.

**Key relationship:** T(n)=2T(n/2)+n → Θ(n log n)

examGuide.title: A repeatable solving procedure
examGuide.body:
1. Identify subproblem count and shrink factor.
2. Sum work per level.
3. Check theorem hypotheses and base conditions.

examGuide.title: Approach the exam question
examGuide.body: Identify whether a recurrence reduces n by a constant, a ratio, or a nonlinear transform. Master theorem requires its stated form and hypotheses. Normalize by an expected leading factor in expressions such as T(n)=√nT(√n)+n; substituting log n can expose the true depth.

examGuide.title: Worked problem
examGuide.body:
T(1)=1 and T(n)=2T(n/2)+n for powers of two. Find T(8).

**Answer: 32.** T(2)=4; T(4)=12; T(8)=32. In general T(n)=n(1+log₂n), giving Θ(n log n). Each of the log₂n nonleaf levels contributes n work, and leaves contribute n.

examGuide.title: Conditions and edge cases
examGuide.body:
Master theorem does not directly apply to T(n−1) or T(√n). Fit initial conditions before discarding characteristic-root terms.

Do not apply the Master theorem to T(n)=T(n−1)+n.

examGuide.title: Worked question patterns
examGuide.body:
#### Pattern 1 · MCQ

T(n)=2T(n/2)+n with constant base has order:

- **A.** Θ(n²)
- **B.** Θ(log n)
- **C.** Θ(n)
- **D.** Θ(n log n)

**Answer: D.** Each of Θ(log n) nonleaf levels costs n, giving Θ(n log n).

#### Pattern 2 · MSQ

Choose true statements.

- **A.** T(n−1)+1 is not in the standard Master form
- **B.** Recursion depth alone gives total work
- **C.** T(n)=T(n/2)+1 has Θ(log n) work
- **D.** Leaves may dominate a recursion tree

**Answer: A, C, D.** Depth ignores branching and per-node work, refuting B. The other statements follow from recursive work accounting.

#### Pattern 3 · NAT

T(1)=1, T(n)=T(n/2)+1 for powers of two. Find T(32).



**Answer: 6.** Arguments are 32,16,8,4,2,1. Five increments plus base value one give six.

#### Pattern 4 · NAT · Transfer problem

T(1)=1 and T(n)=4T(n/2)+n² for powers of two. Find T(8).



**Answer: 256.** T(2)=4+4=8; T(4)=4·8+16=48; T(8)=4·48+64=256. Each of three nonleaf levels costs 64 and the 64 leaves contribute another 64.

examGuide.title: Work through the supplied PYQs
examGuide.body:
#### GATE 2026 CS2 · Q25 · MSQ

[Open the original question and try it](/#/lesson/algorithm-recurrences?tab=practice)

**What is tested:** Divide-and-conquer recurrence analysis. Refer to the original image for complete givens and diagrams.

1. A sums one unit across n−1 recursive decrements, giving T(n)=n. B’s recursion tree has Θ(n) constant-cost nodes, also giving Θ(n).
2. C adds n work on each of Θ(log n) levels: Θ(n log n). D sums n+(n−1)+…+1: Θ(n²).
3. The linear recurrences are **A,B**.

#### GATE 2024 CS1 · Q42 · MCQ

[Open the original question and try it](/#/lesson/algorithm-recurrences?tab=practice)

**What is tested:** Divide-and-conquer recurrence analysis. Refer to the original image for complete givens and diagrams.

1. For T(n)=√n·T(√n)+n, divide by n and put U(n)=T(n)/n. Then U(n)=U(√n)+1.
2. Repeated square roots reduce log n by a factor of two per level, so there are Θ(log log n) nontrivial levels.
3. Thus U(n)=Θ(log log n) and **T(n)=Θ(n log log n), A**.
